input.quote: Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Section 9 provides only for-cause (9.1), insolvency (9.2) and security/service-failure (9.3) termination rights, and there is no Section 9.4 or any other Customer termination-for-convenience right in the Agreement. With a three-year term and a USD 2,000,000 annual take-or-pay commitment, the absence of any Customer convenience right is walk-away territory, so the fallback is not met. We insert a single new Section 9.4 at the preferred level: Customer convenience termination on 30 days' prior written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, and no Vendor convenience right during a committed term. No other clause is disturbed.

ops.text: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience upon 30 days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall provide a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a committed term.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The term runs three years with no Customer exit without cause, so we have added a Customer termination-for-convenience right on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, and confirmed Vendor has no convenience right during a committed term.
proposal.summary: Insert Section 9.4: Customer termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees; no Vendor convenience right during a committed term

mappings.element: No more than 30 days' written notice.
No Vendor termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
